choices.content: Is as far from \(\overline{AB}\) as from \(D\)

question.prompt: \(\overline{AB}\) is a fixed diameter of a circle whose center is \(O.\) From \(C,\) any point on the circle, a chord \(\overline{CD}\) is drawn perpendicular to \(\overline{AB}.\) Then, as \(C\) moves over a semicircle, the bisector of angle \(OCD\) cuts the circle in a point that always:

solutions.explanation:
Assume first that \(C\) is neither \(A\), \(B\), nor the midpoint of its semicircular arc, so the chord and angle are nondegenerate. We seek the circle intersection of the internal angle-bisector ray other than \(C\).

Let \(P\) be the endpoint of the diameter perpendicular to \(AB\) on the opposite side of \(AB\) from \(C\). This is a fixed point as \(C\) moves within either semicircle determined by \(AB\). Since \(OP\) and \(CD\) are both perpendicular to \(AB\), they are parallel.

The radii \(OC\) and \(OP\) are equal, so triangle \(OCP\) is isosceles and
\[
\angle OCP=\angle CPO.
\]
Because \(P\) is on the opposite side of \(AB\) from \(C\), the parallel lines give
\[
\angle CPO=\angle PCD.
\]
Thus \(CP\) makes equal angles with \(CO\) and \(CD\). These equal angles are base angles of the nondegenerate isosceles triangle, so each is less than \(90^\circ\). Consequently, \(CP\) is the internal bisector of \(\angle OCD\), and its second circle intersection is \(P\).

Finally,
\[
\angle AOP=\angle POB=90^\circ,
\]
so the corresponding arcs \(AP\) and \(PB\) are equal. Hence \(P\) bisects the semicircular arc \(AB\) opposite \(C\).

There are exceptional positions in the literal statement. At \(C=A\) or \(C=B\), the perpendicular line is tangent and the chord collapses, so \(\angle OCD\) is undefined. At the midpoint of the moving semicircular arc, the rays \(CO\) and \(CD\) coincide. If these positions are interpreted by limits, the second intersection remains the same fixed point \(P\). Therefore the answer is choice A with the recorded nondegeneracy or limiting convention.
solutions.title: Identify the fixed point using equal angles
